author: WP02
summary: A short appendix listing the documentation's pinned repository set with roles, the 23 physical module directories with their ownership, the renderer module tree in clusters, and the audit's contamination-control method. The module list is current at TARGET; the pins are documentation history and the claim that gates reject undeclared dependencies is overstated. The repository roles are preserved on the ecosystem deep dive and the module table on the Development repository map; the renderer clusters were added to the module-architecture deep dive.

concepts.text: The appendix records the source boundary and module topology of its edition, with sibling pins retained from earlier audits unless a claim needed a newer state.
concepts.note: Documentation methodology of the source text; the site pins every statement to 009d40f5 and names sibling revisions per claim.

concepts.text: cna is pinned at the documentation's own commit, a development snapshot later than the alpha.1 tag.
concepts.note: The site documents snapshot 009d40f5, not the source text's earlier pin.

concepts.text: sharp-runtime is the .NET-shaped foundation CNA builds on; the alpha.1 release recorded its own sharp-runtime build revision separately from any audit pin.
easy-gl is the shared implementation beneath the five EasyGL profiles.
tokens: five public identities sharing one CNA implementation factory

concepts.text: meta-gl is the typed GL layer consumed by easy-gl and is not a CNA renderer identity.
free-direct provides DirectDraw, DirectSound and DirectPlay-shaped compatibility used by FREEDIRECT and the Speedy Blupi work.
free-api is the narrow Win32-shaped support layer consumed by free-direct.
xna4-spec is a converted XNA documentation inventory: an authority aid, not a behaviour oracle.
cna-samples is the translated official-sample catalogue and cna-examples the CNA-native demonstration catalogue; both are consumer evidence.
cna-template is a minimal downstream skeleton, cna-extended an extension library outside the core API, and CNA Craft a larger desktop and web consumer.
The specific short revisions listed for each repository (easy-gl, meta-gl, free-direct, free-api, xna4-spec and the consumers).
concepts.note: Pins of the source text's audit; the ecosystem page records the revisions read for its own statements.

concepts.text: The root version remains 0.1.0-alpha.1; the product string, the preceding tag and a later source snapshot serve different purposes.

concepts.text: CMake accepts a caller-supplied sharp-runtime root rather than enforcing a recorded SHA.
tokens: No part of CNA checks which sharp-runtime commit it got

concepts.text: The top-level module directories at TARGET are core, math, design, platform, runtime, graphics, graphics-ext, renderers, input, audio, media, video-ffmpeg, content, content-pipeline, storage, devices, devices-ext, gamer-services, net, phone, diagnostics, inspector and c-api, each with its stated ownership.
Production sources, public and public-internal headers, tests and examples live with their owning module.

The claim that CMake boundary gates reject misplaced translation units and undeclared dependencies is half true: misplaced TUs fail the configure, but undeclared link edges are caught only by fifteen probe closures that no workflow evaluates.
tokens: By reading, no workflow evaluates a link-closure contract

concepts.text: core holds root helpers, versioning and framework primitives (including the generated version header).
phone is the Windows Phone-shaped lifecycle and notification surface, outside the umbrella and outside the C ABI's link set.
diagnostics provides OFF/STATS/FULL metrics, zones and recordings, and inspector the optional authenticated agent with bridge and UI.

The aggregate CNA target composes the enabled framework modules, platform, the default renderer (every compiled family in shared mode) and dependencies; narrow aliases serve closure tests; the pipeline, Inspector and C API are not pulled into a game silently.
concepts.note: The static umbrella names only the default renderer target; others arrive through graphics' private edges.

concepts.text: modules/renderers contains common plus 21 family directories in seven clusters: GL-shaped, explicit/platform GPU, Direct3D, abstraction, native or portable 2D, browser 2D and non-GPU.
Only EasyGL maps more than one identity to a family, and the physical tree alone does not prove that a selector is admissible on a host or that an operation works.
tokens: which is why the registry has 25 identities and the tree 21 families
every renderer dependency is available on this host

concepts.text: The audit used clean detached BASE and TARGET worktrees, never the owner's moving checkout, and repeated the TARGET-to-checkout diff at completion.
concepts.note: Contamination-control method of the documentation audit; not CNA technical knowledge.

concepts.text: A later edition should start from the pinned range, derive modules and identities from source, classify dependencies, evidence peers and consumers separately and keep sibling pins until a claim needs more.

concepts.text: Dependencies (siblings), references that are read but never linked, and consumers that pin their own revisions are different kinds of repository and must be classified separately.
